content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper authors propose to combine end-to-end TTS and (voice conversion) VC modules for zero-shot operation. The key innovation presented in this paper is to form a joint dictionary based content representation for both modes of operation. Here they utilize VQVAE methodology, with an additional loss to try to keep both representations as close as possible.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Key strength in this paper is the unified content representation, whether coming from annotated text (for TTS) or ASR -type model in VC operation. This idea is quite nice. 

About weaknesses, I find that paper does not really train a VC model, as in Eq (9), there is no specific component to change the speaker representation from i to j, which is the whole point of VC. It also shows in the experiments where authors have not really objectively evaluated VC performance. 

I would have expected to see more experimental analysis from this kind of experimental paper. 

As an additional point, I would like to make is that paper does have a bit of putting known blocks together approach.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Paper needs serious rewriting for clarity and finalization. Some places such as in Section 3.2, what is this Eq reference "is a sequence of continuous vector in Eq. " just as an example of lack of finalization.
content.summary_of_the_review: Interesting core idea to join TTS and VC into one module, but paper does not appear to be in finalized state. Experiments need to be made more rigorous and problems in the definition of VC needs to be fixed.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

display_title: Official Review of Paper4110 by Reviewer 8rQ4

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes UnifySpeech, the unified framework for TTS and VC. The proposed system has 3 different modules to model linguistic content, speaker identity, and prosody information separately. UnifySpeech introduces the vector quantization (VQ) method to project the outputs of the text encoder for TTS and the content encoder for VC into the same space. The unified framework has the advantage that unlabeled speech can be used for speech synthesis.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths

* Propose a unified framework for TTS and VC tasks by using VQ methods to the output of text encoders and content encoders.
* Easy to understand

Weaknesses

* (1) Their experimental results do not sufficiently show the advantages of the proposed unified framework. 
* (1.1) The speaker similarity metric used in the results of Table 1 and Table 2 is insufficient to represent how similar the speaker is to the reference speaker. In general, it is better to provide subjective evaluation results for speaker similarity mean opinion score as well, and the results should be provided through demos or samples. 
* (1.2) In Table 4, there is no comparison with other TTS models and VC models except for the ablated setup of UnifySpeech. Also, it is better to provide not only the averaged value of MOS but also a 95% confidence interval for reliability. 
* (1.3) This work only provides the samples for VC and not for TTS in the Supplementary Material, which is necessary to show that unifying the VC task is beneficial for TTS.
* (1.4) There is no explanation for the evaluation setup. (ex. the number of unseen speakers for evaluation, the number of sentences for evaluation, ...)
* (2) This work might be the first work that uses the VQ method for the purpose of unifying TTS and VC, but the method itself is not new. (ex. NaturalSpeech [1] introduces VQ to the output of the phoneme encoder.)
* (3) No ablation study for the number of codes in the codebook. (For the small value of |V|, the codebook's capacity is not enough to represent all the phonemes. For the higher value of |V|, the codebook will contain more information than pronunciation. These kinds of analysis are required.)

Comments
* To show that UnifySpeech can perform zero-shot TTS or VC, it is required to show the performance of zero-shot adaptation for unseen speakers in large-scale datasets (LibriTTS). 
* Typo - higer (in abstract) -> higher | Figure 4 description
* Wrong citation - In page 6, hifigan (Lei et al., 2022) as vocoder ->  (hifigan : Kong et al., 2020)
* Learnable codebook in Figure 1 and Figure 2 can be improved. 

References
[1] Tan et al., NaturalSpeech: End-to-End Text to Speech Synthesis with Human-Level Quality
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity, Quality - Their experimental results do not show the advantages of UnifySpeech. (Lack of explanation for the evaluation and ablation studies)
Novelty - VQ method can be a good choice for unifying TTS and VC, but the method is not quite new. 
Reproducibility - There is little explanation for the hyperparameter values.
content.summary_of_the_review: To show the advantages of the proposed framework, the paper should provide more diverse experiments and justified results. Experiment results and their explanations are very scarce. The details of the paper should be further improved.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

display_title: Official Review of Paper4110 by Reviewer CKPa

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes UnifySpeech to boost the performance of text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC) simultaneously. Since for TTS, the speech content information is from the text, and for VC it's from the source speech, UnifySpeech uses separate content extraction modules in the two pipelines while all the remaining units are shared. Vector quantization and domain constrain are also applied to bridge the gap between the content domains of TTS and VC.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
It's an interesting idea to bring TTS and VC into one single pipeline. However, it's not convincing enough that this unified framework is beneficial to those two tasks. The author argued that UnifySpeech can handle zero-shot TTS and zero-shot VC. But I didn't find any zero-shot algorithms, experiment results and analysis in this paper. Actually it's not clear how UnifySpeech can handle the zero-shot cases, since the content features in those two pipelines are extracted by different encoders (text encoder in TTS and content encoder in VC). So it's more like a multi-task training pipeline.

The major challenge that VC tasks are facing is the content and timbre disentanglement. Considering the vector quantization module used in this paper already has certain capability to remove the timbre information from content by itself, it's not clear whether the TTS joint training or vector quantization contributes to the feature disentanglement for VC task. Based on the MOS  result, TTS joint training actually makes VC perform worse. Another related question is, in section 4.4, what's the speaker embedding visualization for VC w/o TTS? Will that make the speaker embeddings totally NOT distinguishable? 

On the other hand, the normal VC-only training doesn't require any labelled text and speech pair, which makes VC enjoy the benefit of large-scale training. However, the joint training pipeline requires the VC task to have paired text and speech. From this point of view, it actually makes the VC task more challenging and labelled data dependent.

Also, it's not clear how the VC is helping TTS. The MOS only shows marginal improvement when jointly train TTS with VC (MOS improvement is 0.04). TTS task naturally enjoys the advantage of content and timbre disentanglement, since text information is independent with speaker identity. However, VC makes TTS face the risk of timbre leakage in content features.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: I am not convinced by the benefits of TTS and VC joint training, and the zero-shot algorithms and results are missing.
content.summary_of_the_review: Based on the experiment results provided by this paper, the TTS and VC joint training didn't significantly improve the performance of those two tasks. More appealing results are needed to show the benefits of this unified framework.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
